diagnostic:
Review correction, S1 implementation: both findings owned by implementation are fixed, and the whole offer behaviour is unchanged.

Finding 2, the Send-test refusal's authorization reads. The refusal no longer builds a Viewer. NoConnectionCause now owns one private in_the_workspace(manages_the_workspace) that returns the sentence and the workspace's own way out of it, the two parts nothing outside the workspace can change; the new public sentence(viewer_is_workspace_admin) returns the first of them, and words(Viewer) composes the same pair with the viewer's setup offer. So the independence the reviewer observed, that is_instance_admin only ever feeds fixes and never a byte of the sentence, is now structural rather than a comment: sentence is never given the fact, so it cannot read it. matrix_setup.rs calls cause.sentence(door.target.viewer_is_workspace_admin), a bool the door's view already holds, and performs no store read; the single remaining instance-admin read on that path is the one refused_page's own nav does, which restores the US-IIS-04 Technical Note and design constraint K4 (no added query). Caller::viewer in handlers/mod.rs lost its only caller and is deleted with the change, as CODING_STANDARDS' dead-code rule requires.

Deviation to report, for the architect. The S1 impact record for matrix_setup.rs:281 says that door "keeps doing so through the Viewer". It no longer does: it passes the one workspace-role fact instead. I followed the reviewer's named remediation because the design's own K4 forbids the extra read that the Viewer route costs there, so the two design statements could not both hold; D2's objection to bare bools was about an agreement on argument position across five call sites of words, line and project_lines, which this single-fact, single-caller accessor does not create. If the architect wants the Viewer shape back on that door, the reconciliation is theirs, not a second document from me.

Finding 3, the five viewer-dependent-looking empty offers. Viewer::offers now has exactly one caller, SharedConnection::line's Connected arm, where the viewer genuinely decides whether Manage workspace integrations is offered; offers_with_setup is replaced by setup_offer, which answers only I-19 and only for an instance admin. Every place with no workspace fix states the empty offer directly: the Lost and Unreadable lines and the lead branch of project_lines build Vec::new(), the admin branch builds its single link outright, and words builds Vec::from_iter(workspace_fix) and extends it with the setup offer only inside the awaits_this_foundry branch. The ordering invariant stays constructive: the workspace link is pushed first and I-19 appended last, inside the instance-admin branch only, so neither an inverted order nor an I-19 for a non-instance-admin is constructible through words.

Verification, each declared command run once in the Lima VM foundry-test with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 exported inside the VM shell and a timeout bound, on the corrected tree. foundry-app library check exit 0, 4 passed, 0 failed, 197 filtered out, with the 56-row (offer, connected, viewer) table and the project table unchanged, so the whole finite relation still holds after the restructure. eip_warm then eip_lane us-iis-04 exit 0, 19 scenarios (19 passed), 195 steps (195 passed); the lane carried the acceptance designer's parallel feature-file addition, which this run picked up and which passes. eip_lane integrations-wayfinding exit 0, 54 scenarios (54 passed), 400 steps (400 passed), the same counts as the before-move, after-move and implementation observations. rustfmt --check on the three edited files reports no diff.
